parole.significato: A group of people supporting the same thing or person.
parole.testo: From Latin cohors (stem cohort-); borrowed into Old English as coorta, but reintroduced into Middle English as cōhort and chōors via Old French cohorte. Doublet of court.

parole.significato: A kind of carriage like a gig, originally of wickerwork.
parole.testo: From Old English Crogedene ("saffron valley"), from Old English croh (“saffron”) (< Latin crocus (“saffron”)) + Old English denu (“valley”).

parole.significato: A privilege of setting up, and moving about, sheepfolds, in any fields within manors, in order to manure them or to kee…
parole.testo: From Latin faldagium, from Old English fald (whence English fold). Compare foldage.

parole.significato: To take precedence or superiority over; to preside over.
parole.testo: From fore- (“before”) + sit, sometimes as a calque of Latin praesideō or Old English foresittan.

parole.significato: A member of the Germanic tribe that existed in modern-day Denmark that invaded England about the same time as the Angle…
parole.testo: From Latin plural Iuti, Iutae (in Bede), from Old English Ēotas. Ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *eut, from Proto-Germanic *eutaz, *eutaniz. The spelling was later influenced by Medieval Latin Jutae, Juti.
From Latin portgrevius, from Old English portgerēfa, from port + gerēfa (“reeve”).

parole.significato: One of a particular English breed of small sheep with long wool and horns.
parole.testo: From a name of a village in Kent (see Old Romney), from a compound of Latin rumen (“gullet”) and Old English ēa (“river”).

parole.significato: A loft or upper chamber forming the private accommodation of the head of the household in a medieval hall; a garret roo…
parole.testo: From Middle English solar, soler; from a conflation of Old English soler, solere (“raised platform; loft, upper room, upper part of a house, soler”), from Latin sōlārium; and Old English solor, salor (“residence, dwelling; hall; palace”), from Proto-West Germanic *salaʀ, from Proto-Germanic *salaz,
